source_claims: Original v1 is a Lifelong Agents at ICLR 2026 workshop paper, not an assertion of main-conference acceptance.

Per-input LoRA selection uses sequential sampling without replacement; actual ordered path log-probability includes conditional denominators. Output coefficients are fixed and equal for selected adapters.

RLOO uses M independent complete selections for the same input, M >= 2, a leave-one-out baseline, and 1/(M-1) when centering by the full-sample mean. The note correctly stops advantage gradients and does not claim convergence.
The top-k result assumes a given optimal subset already has sampling probability strictly above one half; it is not a training-success or whole-network global-optimality guarantee.

The initialization arithmetic is correctly restricted to the printed Gaussian-initialization bound and Rademacher input norm 32. The note does not infer that the paper's actual event probability is false.
Table 4 yields 10.2793% extra per-step time and 21.1380% extra total time. The note distinguishes these and makes no p-bit power inference.
The 0.070B parameter figure is the average of task-specific configurations; the note distinguishes activated versus stored/trainable parameter ambiguity and identifies missing reproduction details.

M is training rollout count, k is active adapters, and correlated finite-chain inference observations S are different. The note correctly requires actual finite CTMC path probabilities rather than equilibrium Softmax probabilities.
